hook: Bun's own test count says node:http passes 403 of 415 tests, and Node's own calendar says v20 died on 24 March 2026. Neither runtime charges a cent, so the bill arrives somewhere else.

sections.title: Both runtimes cost nothing, so the invoice arrives as labour
sections.content:
Bun is MIT. Node.js is MIT. Neither sells a paid tier, so the bill is engineer-hours on three meters: the release calendar, the compatibility surface and the native-module ABI.

> For teams maintaining a Node service: as of 10 November 2026, both runtimes have no price.

- **Node:** Node publishes a release calendar; v26 Lithium, v24 Krypton and v22 Jod are LTS.
- **Bun:** 1.4.0 (20 August 2026) combined the Rust rewrite with the compatibility-target move from 24.3.0 to 26.3.0 and native ABI 147.

Identify whether each native addon uses stable Node-API or a version-specific V8/native ABI; test the actual package on Bun, OS and architecture.

sections.title: Node bills you on a date you did not choose
sections.content:
Node's release page reads like a work schedule:

| Major | Status | Key date |
|---|---|---|
| v27 | Alpha | first released 29 Oct 2026 |
| v26 Lithium | LTS | first released 5 May 2026 |
| v25 | EOL | 31 Mar 2026 |
| v24 Krypton | LTS | first released 6 May 2025 |
| v22 Jod | LTS | first released 24 Apr 2024 |
| v20 Iron | EOL | 24 Mar 2026 |

Support window and release cycle:

1. LTS "typically guarantees that critical bugs will be fixed for a total of 30 months" (Node's wording).
2. Starting with v27, the cycle becomes annual: every major gets six months of Alpha, six of Current, then LTS.

Read it as a penalty table. It punishes the team that adopts a major and forgets it: v20 lived from 17 Apr 2023 to 24 Mar 2026, about 35 months.

> If production still runs Node 20, plan a move to Node 24 or 26 LTS: Node 20 reached EOL on 24 March 2026.

sections.title: Who should not pick Node for unbuilt TypeScript
sections.content:
Type stripping is on by default, stable since v25.2.0 / v24.12.0. Node executes erasable syntax without type checking; other syntax needs separate tooling.

```ts
// runs on Node 26 with no flags: every annotation here is erasable
type Host = string;
const host: Host = process.env.HOST ?? "localhost";
console.log(`binding ${host}`);
```

> `enum` throws `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX`.

Node 26 also refuses:

- `namespace` with runtime code, parameter properties, import aliases: same error
- `.tsx` files
- `paths`, because `tsconfig.json` is ignored
- TypeScript inside `node_modules`
- parsing without WebAssembly: `ERR_WEBASSEMBLY_NOT_SUPPORTED`

This meter punishes codebases built on enums and path aliases; for them, the build step stays.

sections.title: Bun's own node:http count leaves 415 − 403 = 12 tests failing
sections.content:
Bun says it plainly: "Bun is not 100% compatible with Node.js yet." Bun's own 1.4 counts against the Node 26.3.0 suite:

| Module | Bun 1.4 passes | Not passing |
|---|---|---|
| node:http | 403 / 415 | 415 − 403 = 12 |
| node:fs | 349 / 358 | 358 − 349 = 9 |
| node:module | 68 / 93 | 93 − 68 = 25 |
| node:test_runner | 28 / 81 | 81 − 28 = 53 |
| node:inspector | 22 / 110 | 110 − 22 = 88 |
| node:sqlite | 18 / 18 | 18 − 18 = 0 |

On node:http that is 12 ÷ 415 ≈ 2.9%, the failing 3%. Bun says 1.4 made 1,517 more Node tests pass.

> Native compatibility is not one blanket rebuild rule. Node-API provides ABI stability across Node versions, unlike addons tied to V8 or a version-specific native ABI. Bun implements Node-API independently, so Node-API compatibility and package dependencies still need testing; a Node version number alone does not prove a rebuild is required.

Check required inspector APIs; module pass counts are not application coverage.

sections.title: Who should not pick Bun: teams requiring missing APIs
sections.content:
Bun's compatibility docs name the gaps. Map each to a service you run:

- **HTTP servers tuned for a load balancer.** `http.Server` does not extend `net.Server`, the `keepAlive` / `keepAliveInitialDelay` server options are no-ops, and `listen(handle)` is ignored. Your keep-alive tuning silently does nothing.
- **mTLS and multi-tenant TLS.** node:https lacks `getPeerCertificate()` and `getCipher()` and does not support `SNICallback`. Retain Node if you require these APIs.
- **Signing code.** BoringSSL-backed node:crypto lacks `ed448`, `x448`, `rsa-pss` and `dsa` keys, has no `secp256k1` curve and no `chacha20-poly1305`.
- **APM tracing.** `async_hooks` `createHook` is a stub and async ids are always 0; correlation by async id collapses.
- **`cluster` fleets on macOS or Windows.** HTTP load-balancing across workers only works on Linux, via `SO_REUSEPORT`.

> `AsyncLocalStorage` context does not propagate into Worker/BroadcastChannel events in Bun.

sections.title: Bun stays MIT after Anthropic's acquisition; check before migrating
sections.content:
Anthropic acquired Bun on 2 December 2025. Claude Code ships as a Bun executable (Bun's statement), and Bun's founder wrote then: "Today, Bun makes $0 in revenue." Bun stays MIT.

The acquisition changes who pays for Bun's roadmap. It does not change the licence, and it does not change the API surface you have to test.

Check today:

1. List every `.node` addon, identify Node-API versus version-specific ABI dependencies, and test supported binaries on the target runtime, OS and architecture.
2. Check required HTTP APIs, `createHook`, distinct async IDs, `getPeerCertificate` and `SNICallback` against Bun's gaps.
3. Write down the EOL date of the Node major running in production.

decision_matrix.situation: HTTP service considering Bun after checking required server APIs
decision_matrix.pick: Bun only if required APIs are supported and the service passes its checks; otherwise retain Node
decision_matrix.why: Bun's own node:http count is 403 / 415; check unsupported server options, http.Server inheritance and listen(handle), not just the pass count.

decision_matrix.situation: Repo with native addons built for Node 24
decision_matrix.pick: Test addon API and runtime compatibility before migrating
decision_matrix.why: Stable Node-API addons are not automatically invalidated by a Node major change. V8/legacy addons can require compatible builds; Bun support and external dependencies must be checked per package.

decision_matrix.situation: Production tracing agent requiring createHook or distinct async IDs
decision_matrix.why: Keep Node if your tracing agent requires createHook or distinct async IDs: Bun documents the hook as a stub and async IDs as always 0.

decision_matrix.situation: TLS gateway requiring getPeerCertificate() or SNICallback
decision_matrix.why: Bun's node:https lacks getPeerCertificate() and does not support SNICallback.

decision_matrix.situation: Signing service that needs secp256k1 or ed448 keys
decision_matrix.why: Bun's BoringSSL-backed node:crypto has no secp256k1 curve and no ed448 key type.

decision_matrix.pick: Node 24 or 26 LTS, not a runtime switch
decision_matrix.why: v20 reached EOL on 24 March 2026, and an LTS move fixes that without adding Bun's compatibility gaps to the same sprint.

decision_matrix.situation: Healthy service on Node 22 Jod with no pain points
decision_matrix.why: v22 is still LTS and was last updated 20 October 2026, so no date forces a move yet.

decision_matrix.situation: Internal scripts and CLIs that currently pull in a separate test runner, linter and formatter
decision_matrix.why: Bun 1.4 ships bun test --parallel, bun lint, bun fmt and bun check in the same binary.

cost_math.label: Bun 1.4 node:http compatibility gap
cost_math.result: 12 failing node:http tests, about 3% (Bun's own count; neither runtime has a price, so the unit is tests)

cost_math.label: Debug-and-test loop gap in Bun 1.4
cost_math.result: Bun's own counts leave 88 inspector tests and 53 test-runner tests unpassed; check the APIs your debugger or test runner requires before migrating.

cost_math.label: Node 20 EOL-to-LTS decision
cost_math.formula: 17 Apr 2023 → 24 Mar 2026 ≈ 35 months from first release to EOL; this is not the LTS fix window
cost_math.result: Move production off EOL Node 20 to Node 24 or 26 LTS; the documented 30-month LTS fix guarantee is a separate interval.

verdict_summary: Pick Node if your service needs an API Bun documents as missing — getPeerCertificate(), SNICallback, createHook with real async ids — or if a required native addon fails on the target runtime. Pick Bun if the addons and APIs you depend on survive its 403-of-415 node:http count, because the runtime itself will never appear on an invoice.

faqs.a: No: type stripping performs no type checking, so a separate tool is still required. Decorators are a parser error, and `--experimental-transform-types` was removed in v26.0.0.

Bun's own `hello.js` benchmark puts Linux start-up at 5.1 ms for Bun 1.4 versus 27.2 ms for Node.js 26; these are vendor measurements, not independent ones. Separately, Bun's peak-memory figures under load, with 1,000,000 requests and 64 connections, put the Vite dev server at 233 MB on Bun versus 214 MB on Node, so Bun is not lighter everywhere.

faqs.q: Can I buy support for a Node major after LTS ends?
faqs.a: Not from the Node.js project itself. Commercial support past Maintenance LTS is sold by OpenJS Ecosystem Sustainability Program partners.

faqs.q: Does Bun's MIT licence cover everything in the binary?
faqs.a: No: Bun statically links JavaScriptCore/WebKit, which is LGPL-2. That is why Bun's licence file spells out relinking obligations.

tool_b.tagline: The runtime with a published release calendar
tool_b.db: Node core plus the npm ecosystem
tool_b.pricing: Free · MIT · support past Maintenance LTS via OpenJS partners
tool_b.realtime: node:http servers, cluster workers, inspector for tracing

pros: A dated calendar: v26 Lithium and v24 Krypton are LTS, and LTS typically guarantees fixes for 30 months
Native addons are the default path, and ABI builds target the runtime you actually run
TypeScript type stripping runs with no build step for erasable syntax

migration_guide: Classify native addons by Node-API versus version-specific V8/native ABI, then test actual binaries on Bun and Node for your OS and architecture. Rebuild or replace only incompatible packages. Exercise required HTTP, TLS and async-hooks APIs before changing production runtimes.
